# team-flowise
English | 中文
A multi-agent team plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Define roles, wire them into a node graph, run it —
plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Define roles, wire them into a node graph, run it — and watch it work.
One agent is fine until the job has parts. Then you want a planner, a coder, a reviewer, and someone
to check the numbers. This gives you those, runs them in dependency order, lets a reviewer send wor
k back, and shows you which step is stuck.
- **Roles are records.** Name, persona, model route, tool preset, timeout. Create them in Settings,

or from a conversation with `team_create_agent`.
- **The graph decides the order.** Nodes declare `d

ependsOn`; everything that is ready runs in the same wave, in parallel.
- **Review is a gate, not a
suggestion.** A node can name its own reviewer. Blocking findings go back to the worker verbatim, an

d rework is bounded — two rounds per node, three per run.
- **Runs stick around.** Roles, workflows,
the task ledger and run history live in four durable storage domains. A run cut off by a crash come

s back marked interrupted rather than quietly repainted as finished.
- **A flaky step does not cost
you the pipeline.** A worker that dies for an infrastructure reason is re-dispatched automatically;

a run that ended short can be continued, reusing the nodes that succeeded.
- **You can watch it.** T
he right sidebar carries the graph, each role's progress, and — for the node you select — the model,

reasoning effort, output cap and persona it actually ran with, plus the reviewer's verdict.
- **And
you can clean up after it.** Every list in Settings has a delete control, so a stale role or a fini
shed run does not need a conversation with an agent to remove.
[该节后续省略]
## Screenshots
**Roles.** Every stored role, with the model route it will run under.
**Task board.** Each node of a run becomes one ledger task, so the board *is* the run's state. `it1`
means first attempt.
**Run progress.** The graph and its waves, each role's progress, and what the selected node actually
ran with. The run below is this plugin building its own UI.
## Install
Two clients, two different ways in. Use the one you have.
### `dsh` on your PATH (the CLI, or `dsh web`)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or the prebuilt package, which needs no git — but install it from the **path you downloaded it to**,
ckage, which needs no git — but install it from the **path you downloaded it to**, not from its URL:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That distinction is not pedantry. On pnpm 10 an `https` tarball-**URL** dependency fails permanently
once pnpm's store holds that URL:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It is not a network blip: it reproduces on a second install into a second profile sharing the store,
for a version-free `latest/` URL and a version-pinned one alike, and deleting the lockfile does not
recover it (only a fresh store does). Local files and git specs are unaffected. That is why every c
ommand on this page uses the git spec.
There is no build step, and nothing to approve. Install into a profile that has a web app, so you ac
tually get the UI. (The plugin mounts in a bare profile too; you just get no browser half.) Now rest
art dsh — host code and the client bundle are both read at startup, so nothing is live until you do.
### DSH Desktop (the packaged app)
There is no `dsh` command to run here: the app carries the harness inside itself and owns its profil
e, so **its own plugin panel is the install surface** — this plugin shows up there once the catalog
lists it. The market's own button installs `github:Drkoh-wz/team-craft#path:/packages/team-flowise`,
which pnpm resolves to an **ssh** URL (`git+ssh://git@github.com/...`); on a machine without GitHub
's ssh host key that fails with `Host key verification failed` inside `resolveGit`, and if git is no
t on the path the Desktop process inherits, it fails with `'git' is not recognized` in the same plac
e. When that happens, one script does the work and never invokes git. Quit Desktop first, then:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It finds the app, refuses to run while Desktop is up (that is what stops its own profile maintenance
from reconciling the change away), picks up the pnpm the app ships, installs this project's publish
ed release package, and lists what to check when you start Desktop again. If Desktop is running but
using a *different* harness home than the one you target, it says so and proceeds — only a real coll
ision is refused. `-Action uninstall`, `-Action check`, `-Spec <anything pnpm accepts>`, `-DryRun` a
nd `-Force` are the rest; `Get-Help .\scripts\install-desktop.ps1 -Full` prints them. It is in the r
elease archive too, under `scripts/`.
[该节后续省略]
### Both
Verified end to end on **DSH Desktop `0.2.0-rc.2`** and the **`dsh` CLI `0.2.0-rc.2`**, on Node 24.
The peer ranges in `packages/team-flowise/package.json` say `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`, and the harness
checks that declaration before it imports the plugin — so a harness that is too old refuses this pl
ugin in one clear line instead of failing in a confusing way later.
Two things worth knowing, because each of them broke this plugin once.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
| **Host half** — `packages/team-flowise/src/index.js` | Registers the `team_*` tools, publishes the

`teamOrchestrator` service, owns the four storage domains, serves `/api/team-flowise/*`. |
| **Clie
nt half** — `packages/team-flowise/src/client/index.js` | The Settings section, the sidebar entry, t

he progress page. |
| **Skill** — `skills/team-flowise/SKILL.md` | Tells an agent when this is worth

. |
| **Skill** — `skills/team-flowise/SKILL.md` | Tells an agent when this is worth reaching for. |
A node is dispatched as a worker subagent carrying the persona, model route and tool preset its role
declares. When it reports back, the node's reviewer is asked for a verdict, and blocking findings b
ecome the next round's feedback. A reviewer that cannot produce a readable verdict is recorded as an
error — and an error never counts as a pass.
